case.title: Mr. Anthony Nkeze v. Registered Trustees of Ikoyi Club 1938

procedural_history.originating_proceedings: Claimant filed suit NICN/LA/430/2012 against the defendant. Judgment was delivered on 21st March, 2014 in favour of the claimant.
procedural_history.procedural_posture: Ruling on motion for stay of execution of judgment pending appeal.

previous_decisions.description: Judgment of the National Industrial Court delivered in favour of the claimant.

interlocutory_applications.application: Motion for stay of execution of judgment pending appeal

appeals.appeal: Appeal filed against the judgment of 21st March, 2014

procedural_events.event: Defendant filed motion for stay of execution.
Ruling delivered granting conditional stay of execution.

material_facts: Judgment was delivered in favour of the claimant on 21st March, 2014.
Defendant filed an appeal against the judgment.
Defendant applied for stay of execution pending appeal.

chronology.event: Judgment delivered in favour of claimant.
Defendant filed motion for stay of execution.
Ruling delivered granting conditional stay of execution.

reliefs_sought.relief: An order staying execution of the judgment of this court delivered on 21st March, 2014 pending the hearing and determination of the Appeal filed against the said judgment.

issues_for_determination.issue: Whether this court should grant a stay of execution in the circumstance of this case.

claimant_arguments: The principles for granting stay of execution require special or exceptional circumstances.
The applicant's affidavit does not disclose special circumstances.
The grounds of appeal are frivolous and do not raise substantial or recondite points of law.
The balance of convenience is not in favour of the defendant.
The defendant participated in the proceedings and did not protest denial of fair hearing.
defendant_arguments: The court has power to grant stay of execution under Section 47 of the National Industrial Court Act, 2006.
The grant of stay is discretionary.
The applicant has a competent and valid appeal raising unanswerable questions of law.
There are special or exceptional circumstances.
The respondent may be unable to refund the judgment sum.
The balance of convenience is in favour of the defendant.
Preservation of the res is necessary to prevent the appeal from being rendered nugatory.

findings_of_law.issue: Power to grant stay of execution
findings_of_law.finding: Section 47 of the National Industrial Court Act, 2006 empowers the court to grant or refuse stay of execution, unconditionally or upon conditions.
Stay of execution will only be granted if there are special or exceptional circumstances.

judicial_analysis.reasoning: The court considered the competing interests of the parties and the guiding principles from appellate courts. It found that a conditional stay of execution was appropriate to preserve the res and prevent the appeal from being rendered nugatory.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether this court should grant a stay of execution in the circumstance of this case.

arguments.claimant: The applicant has not shown special or exceptional circumstances; the grounds of appeal are frivolous; balance of convenience is not in favour of the defendant.
arguments.defendant: The applicant has a valid appeal raising unanswerable questions of law; special circumstances exist; respondent may be unable to refund; balance of convenience is in favour of the defendant.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court reviewed the principles for granting stay of execution, including the need for special or exceptional circumstances. It noted that the court has discretion under Section 47 of the NIC Act to grant a conditional stay. The court compared the competing interests and found that a conditional stay would meet the justice of the case.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: A conditional stay of execution may be granted where the applicant deposits the judgment sum in an interest-yielding account to preserve the res pending appeal.

holdings.issue: Whether this court should grant a stay of execution in the circumstance of this case.

ratio_decidendi.principle: A conditional stay of execution may be granted where the applicant deposits the judgment sum in an interest-yielding account to preserve the res pending appeal.
ratio_decidendi.application: The court ordered the defendant to deposit the judgment sum of N14,204,349.00 in an interest-yielding account opened by the Assistant Chief Registrar within 30 days.

legal_principles.principle: Stay of execution is discretionary and requires special or exceptional circumstances.
legal_principles.context: Application for stay of execution pending appeal.
legal_principles.source: Section 47 of the National Industrial Court Act, 2006; case law.

legal_principles.principle: A conditional stay may be granted by depositing judgment sum in an interest-yielding account.
legal_principles.source: Okin Biscuits v. Oshe [2001] FWLR (pt. 41) p. 1934.

statutory_interpretation.interpretation: The court may order a stay of execution either unconditionally or upon the performance of such conditions as may be imposed in accordance with Rules of Court.
statutory_interpretation.application: The court exercised its discretion to grant a conditional stay.

constitutional_analysis.provision: Section 36 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
constitutional_analysis.application: Claimant argued that defendant participated in proceedings and did not protest denial of fair hearing.

constitutional_analysis.interpretation: Appeals from National Industrial Court to Court of Appeal shall be by leave until National Assembly makes other law.
constitutional_analysis.application: Claimant submitted that appeal is by leave.

precedent_analysis.proposition: Stay of execution will only be granted if there are special or exceptional circumstances.
precedent_analysis.reasoning: Supreme Court held that special or exceptional circumstances are required.

precedent_analysis.authority: T.S.A (Ind.) Ltd v. Kema Investment Ltd [2006] All FWLR (pt. 300) 1564 at 1576
precedent_analysis.proposition: It is not every case where grounds of appeal raise points of law that stay of execution will be granted.
precedent_analysis.reasoning: Ogbuagu JSC held that arguable grounds of appeal are not special circumstances.

precedent_analysis.authority: Okin Biscuits v. Oshe [2001] FWLR (pt. 41) p. 1934
precedent_analysis.proposition: Payment of judgment debt into an interest-yielding account will meet the justice of the case.
precedent_analysis.reasoning: Court held that conditional stay by depositing judgment sum is appropriate.
